newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says U.S. peace envoy due on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Israel says U.S. peace envoy due on Wednesday.

text.p: U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross was expected to arrive in Jerusalem on Wednesday on a new mission to restart stalled Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations, an aide to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday.
"We presume he'll be here the day after tomorrow, on Wednesday, and will again try to facilitate the contacts between the two parties," media adviser David Bar-Illan told Israel Radio's English news.
"I don't think there is any concrete American programme but there is a need and desire to explore the possibilities of finding common grounds between the two partners in these negotiations."

The peace process plunged into crisis in March after Netanyahu gave bulldozers the green light to break ground for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on land claimed by Israel and the Palestinians.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was due to hold talks with Israeli President Ezer Weizman at the Erez border crossing in Gaza on Tuesday to discuss the latest crisis.

On Monday Arafat held talks in Cairo with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and was asked by reporters on his return to Gaza whether he believed Ross was coming with new ideas. "I don't think so," Arafat replied.
Israel Radio asked Bar-Illan whether Israel's demand Arafat fight "terrorism" was still the main item on the agenda for talks with the Palestinians, rather than the issue of resuming peace talks.

"Yes, that is still the case, and frankly I am a little surprised that after the meeting arranged by Dennis Ross last time between the chairman of the Palestinian Authority and our security people..., nothing actually happened," Netanyahu's adviser replied.
